close_reason: GOOD observation acknowledged. localizations migration to HashMap<String, PatchObject> + #[serde(transparent)] on PatchObject is wire-byte-identical and the canonical shape established by JMAP-46s0/JMAP-trmz; matches jmap-tasks-types::Task::localizations and jmap-calendars-types::CalendarEvent::localizations. Test contact_card_localizations_patch_object_transparent (lib.rs) asserts byte-identical round-trip. The HashMap-vs-ordered-map question is the active topic of JMAP-glx8.20 and gets resolved there, but the typed-envelope shape itself is locked in. No code change needed for this bead.
description:
ContactCard.localizations migrated from Option<serde_json::Value> to Option<HashMap<String, PatchObject>>, where jmap_types::PatchObject is #[serde(transparent)] over serde_json::Map<String, Value>. The wire format is byte-identical to the previous Value shape (test: contact_card_localizations_patch_object_transparent at lib.rs:489-502 round-trips a literal JSON string), and the typed shape enforces the outer object-map structure (BCP 47 language tag → PatchObject) at the type system level.

The transparency property is the load-bearing part: a future contributor will be tempted to 'add a discriminant' or 'wrap PatchObject in an enum' or 'just use Value, it's the same thing'. None of those preserve byte-identical wire output. The current shape is the result of bd JMAP-46s0 / JMAP-trmz (the cross-extension PatchObject typed-envelope sweep) and matches the canonical shape in jmap-tasks-types::Task::localizations.

Do not revert to Value, do not change the transparency attribute on PatchObject, do not add wrapper keys.
title: GOOD: localizations typed-envelope migration preserves wire format
